title: “Monks, you should train thus: ‘Our minds will be trained and accumulated as when we went forth; unarisen unwholesome states will not overcome our minds…
content: “Monks, you should train thus: ‘Our minds will be trained and accumulated as when we went forth; unarisen unwholesome states will not overcome our minds and persist; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of impermanence; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of not-self; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of foulness; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of peril; having known the world’s even and uneven, our minds will be trained and accumulated with that perception; having known the world’s arising and passing away, our minds will be trained and accumulated with that perception; having known the world’s origination and cessation, our minds will be trained and accumulated with that perception; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of abandoning; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of dispassion; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of cessation.’ Thus, monks, you should train.”

title: “Cunda, I do not teach merely for the sake of preventing defilements in the present life. Cunda, I do not teach the Dhamma only for…
content: “Cunda, I do not teach merely for the sake of preventing defilements in the present life. Cunda, I do not teach the Dhamma only for the sake of eradicating defilements in the future. Cunda, I teach the Dhamma both for preventing defilements in the present life and for eradicating defilements in the future.”

title: “What do you think, Māgandiya? Have you ever seen or heard of a king or a king’s minister who, while enjoying the five strands of…
content:
“What do you think, Māgandiya? Have you ever seen or heard of a king or a king’s minister who, while enjoying the five strands of sensual pleasure fully and completely, without abandoning craving for sensual pleasures, without removing the fever of sensual pleasures, has dwelt, dwells, or will dwell with craving cut off and mind inwardly peaceful?”
“No, Master Gotama.”

title: “Monks, for any monk or nun whose greed is not abandoned, whose hatred is not abandoned, whose delusion is not abandoned — that one is…
content:
“Monks, for any monk or nun whose greed is not abandoned, whose hatred is not abandoned, whose delusion is not abandoned — that one is called one who has not crossed the ocean with its waves, its whirlpools, its sharks, its demons.

But, monks, for any monk or nun whose greed is abandoned, whose hatred is abandoned, whose delusion is abandoned — that one is called one who has crossed the ocean with its waves, its whirlpools, its sharks, its demons, who has crossed to the far shore, a brahmin standing on dry land.

One who has abandoned greed, hatred, and delusion
Has crossed this ocean with its sharks, demons,
Its terrifying waves — so very hard to cross —
He has passed beyond all bonds.

He has abandoned death,
Without attachments,
He has abandoned suffering,
With no further becoming.
Having reached the goal, he is immeasurable —
I say such a one
Has blinded the King of Death.”

title: “Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain and truly knows: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected:…
content: “Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain and truly knows: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected: ‘He will not attend to the sign of the beautiful. By not attending to the sign of the beautiful, greed will not pollute his mind. He will die without greed, without ill-will, without delusion, without stain, his mind unpolluted.’”

title: Elder Nun Abhirūpa Nandā: Nandā, look at this body — A collection of many diseases, impure, Full of stench, rotting. Develop your mind, Contemplate the…
content:
Elder Nun Abhirūpa Nandā:

Nandā, look at this body —
A collection of many diseases, impure,
Full of stench, rotting.
Develop your mind,
Contemplate the nature of foulness,
Achieve one-pointedness,
With mind well concentrated.

Practice the signless,
Abandon the underlying tendency to conceit.
By fully understanding conceit,
You will live at peace.

title: “Here, monks, a monk reflects, reflects thus: ‘The various sufferings of many kinds that arise in the world, such as aging and death — what…
content:
“Here, monks, a monk reflects, reflects thus: ‘The various sufferings of many kinds that arise in the world, such as aging and death — what is their cause, what is their origin, what gives them birth, what brings them into existence? When what exists does aging and death come to be? When what does not exist does aging and death not come to be?’

Reflecting thus, he understands: ‘The various sufferings of many kinds that arise in the world, such as aging and death — birth is their cause, birth is their origin, birth gives them birth, birth brings them into existence. When birth exists, aging and death come to be. When birth does not exist, aging and death do not come to be.’”

title: “Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain but does not truly know: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can…
content: “Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain but does not truly know: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected: ‘He will attend to the sign of the beautiful. By attending to the sign of the beautiful, greed will pollute his mind. He will die with greed, with ill-will, with delusion, with stain, his mind polluted.’”

title: Hemavata: “Is he without desire for sensual pleasures? Is his mind undisturbed? Has he overcome all delusion? Does he truly have eyes for all things?”…
content:
Hemavata:
“Is he without desire for sensual pleasures?
Is his mind undisturbed?
Has he overcome all delusion?
Does he truly have eyes for all things?”

Sātāgira:
“He has no desire for sensual pleasures,
His mind is undisturbed,
He has overcome all delusion —
The Buddha truly has eyes for all things.”

title: - What closes in the world? Upon what does the world stand? What hangs up the world? What envelops the world? - Death closes in…
content:
- What closes in the world?
Upon what does the world stand?
What hangs up the world?
What envelops the world?
- Death closes in the world,
Upon suffering the world stands,
Craving hangs up the world,
Aging envelops the world.
